data.reasoning_effort: Reasoning effort of the primary model
data.max_tokens: Maximum tokens to return in response

data_description.prompt: Instruct how the LLM should respond. This can be a template.
data_description.llm_hass_api: Allow the model to interact with Home Assistant. Besides the tool list, this is what adds the dump of every exposed entity with its area: without that block, "do I have lights in the bedroom?" is answered badly even though it is not a command.
data_description.chat_model: The Groq model that answers. Groq's quota is per model: 8000 tokens per minute each, counting input plus output.
data_description.reasoning_effort: How much the primary model thinks WHEN it thinks. Qwen family: 'none' or 'default' (careful, 'default' is the maximum). GPT-OSS: 'low', 'medium' or 'high'. Leave it empty to leave it unset: empty is not an error, it is a legitimate value meaning "do not send it", and it is not the same as sending the maximum. This dropdown's vocabulary comes from the family of the model above, and Home Assistant does not redraw the form when you change a dropdown: if you changed the model, save and reopen to see the matching values.
data_description.casa_router_enabled: Before answering, a small model decides whether the query has anything to do with the house. If it says no, the turn goes without tools and saves the 4150 tokens the tool list takes up, which is more than half of the 8000 per minute. When off, and also on any router failure, the tools are sent anyway: losing control of your house is the expensive mistake.
data_description.casa_router_model: The model that answers that question. It gets a 150 token ceiling and 5 seconds, so pick a small, fast one. If you pick one that is also in the fallback chain, both eat the same quota window.
data_description.casa_router_effort: Reasoning effort of the home router. With a 150 token ceiling, thinking too much leaves no room for the three-key JSON it has to return and the answer comes back empty, which counts as a failure. The family minimum is recommended. The vocabulary comes from the family of the model above: if you change it, save and reopen.
data_description.casa_router_threshold: Minimum confidence required to trust it when it says the query is NOT about the house. Below this number the tools are sent anyway. 0.7 is a good starting point.
data_description.razon_router_enabled: Before answering, a small model decides whether the query needs thinking. Off is NOT the same as failure: when off it does reason, with the effort configured above; on a router failure it does not reason, because over-reasoning was what returned empty answers.
data_description.razon_router_model: The model that answers that question. Same 150 token ceiling and 5 seconds as the other router. If you pick one that is also in the fallback chain, both eat the same quota window.
data_description.razon_router_effort: Reasoning effort of the reasoning router. Same problem as the other one: with 150 tokens, thinking too much leaves no budget for the JSON and it comes back empty. The family minimum is recommended. The vocabulary comes from the family of the model above: if you change it, save and reopen.
data_description.razon_router_threshold: Minimum confidence required to trust it when it says reasoning IS needed. Below this number nothing is reasoned, which is the same side a failure falls on.
data_description.model_chain: Models to try, in order, when the main one is out of quota. Groq's limits are per model, so each entry adds its own token-per-minute window. Fallbacks always run without thinking: measured on this installation, the primary answers thinking in 120-180 tokens while the substitute burns its whole 1200 token budget reasoning and comes back empty.
data_description.model_cooldown: Seconds to avoid reusing a model after it was used. It rotates before Groq rejects, saving the round trip of a 429. A model on cooldown is moved to the end of the list, never dropped. Set it to 0 to disable.
data_description.max_tokens: Maximum number of tokens the model can generate in a response. On reasoning models the thinking tokens come out of this same budget: if you leave it short, the answer arrives empty and you hear nothing. If the request still does not fit, the ceiling is halved repeatedly down to a floor of 400 before giving up.
data_description.history_budget: Approximate token budget for the conversation history sent on every request. Groq counts input plus output against the same per-minute limit, and the whole history is resent each turn, so without a budget a long conversation eventually exceeds the limit and then fails permanently. Leave room for max_tokens.
data_description.top_p: Nucleus sampling: consider tokens with top_p probability mass.
data_description.temperature: Higher values make output more random, lower values more deterministic.
data_description.max_retries: Retries the Groq SDK performs on its own after a network error. It is 0 on purpose: rotating through the fallback chain already covers that case, and retrying against the same saturated model only adds seconds to an answer you are going to hear out loud.
